evals.name: investor-numbers
evals.prompt: we're pitching investors next week on our AI contract reviewer. can you check whether the numbers we show are actually trustworthy — the confidence % and 'Verified' badge, the cost-per-query on the dashboard, and the 95% accuracy claim in the README? repo is <fixture>/contractlens. score it 0-10 and tell me what to fix first.

assertions.text: Finds that source_quality and clause_type are read by the scorer but written by nothing, so confidence cannot reach 0.8 and 'Verified' never shows
Finds that recordUsage only runs when debug=1, so the dashboard cost is built on almost no rows
Finds that the usage insert's failure is discarded by .catch(() => {})
Finds that pendingReviews returns 0 on failure, and does not flag documentCount, which handles its failure correctly
Finds that 25 of 40 golden cases hold placeholders (15 runnable) and the threshold of 0 cannot fail, so the 95% claim is unsupported
Finds the while(true) retry around the model call with no cap
Gives a 0-10 score tied to evidence
Each proposed fix says how it was, or would be, made to fail
The fixture is byte-identical after the run

evals.name: bill-doubled
evals.prompt: our LLM bill roughly doubled last week but traffic was flat, and the cost-per-query number on our dashboard just says $0.0000. what's going on? code's at <fixture>/contractlens

assertions.text: Explains the $0.0000: usage is recorded only when debug=1, so there are no rows and cost divides by max(rows,1)
Connects the doubled bill to the uncapped retry that alternates models (a failing first model makes every request pay for at least two calls)
Flags openai/gpt-4-32k as likely retired or failing, or says to check the model ids against the provider catalogue
Notes the call has no output-token cap
Names the data that would confirm or disprove the explanation (provider usage logs, calls per query id)
The fixture is byte-identical after the run
